name: @clossys/designer
description: The designer role: is it well made? A complete visual system — design tokens, theme CSS, accessible React components, icons, charts, and visual quality gates.
author: Clossys

capabilities.subQuestion: Does every token slot resolve to a real, bound value in the consumer's own brand overlay?
capabilities.worldClass: Every token slot this package declares brandable is filled in the consumer's own brand.css, with no typo'd slot name and no silently-unfilled slot.

capabilities.subQuestion: Does every surface consume design values only through bound tokens, never a raw hard-coded value?
capabilities.worldClass: No shipped surface bypasses the token contract with a raw color, size, or spacing value — every design value traces to a token.

capabilities.subQuestion: Is every interface surface composed only from the shared, token-bound component and block library?
capabilities.worldClass: Every interface surface is composed from the shared component and block library — never a bespoke, ungoverned element built outside it.

capabilities.subQuestion: Does every token pairing in use pass its declared contrast ratio?
capabilities.worldClass: Every foreground/background token pairing in use passes its declared WCAG contrast ratio — checked, never assumed.

capabilities.subQuestion: Beyond contrast, does every surface meet its keyboard, semantic, and screen-reader accessibility constraints?
capabilities.worldClass: Every surface is operable by keyboard, exposes correct semantics, and reads correctly to a screen reader — contrast is one axis of accessibility, not the whole of it.

capabilities.subQuestion: Is the type scale governed by one record every surface conforms to?
capabilities.worldClass: Every surface's type usage resolves to one governed type-record scale — never a one-off font-size picked per component; the brand kit and #1210's mark generation both read this record.

capabilities.subQuestion: Does every mount compose only one visual primitive stack, and does its above-the-fold hero conform to its declared fold and hero-CSS contract?
capabilities.worldClass: Every route/surface mount composes exactly one visual primitive stack -- never a mix of design systems assembled under one mount (`surface-ladder.ts`, issues #1055/#1060) -- and its hero renders within its declared fold and hero-CSS contract, checked, never eyeballed per page.

capabilities.subQuestion: Is there one assembled, current brand kit a consumer or Publisher can read whole?
capabilities.worldClass: The brand kit (tokens, type, contrast, components, marks) is one assembled, current record — the web style guide IS the brand kit (#1204), never a second, divergent artifact. Not yet built: today each element (tokens, contrast, type, marks) is checked independently, with nothing that assembles them into one record Publisher can render as the guide page.

capabilities.subQuestion: Does every product get a usable, checked logo and mark variant set without waiting on a hired designer?
capabilities.worldClass: Every product ships a checked mark set (primary, mark, mono, light/dark, favicon, app icons) generated deterministically from its own tokens, or adopted from a supplied mark — contrast, minimum size, clear space, and single-colour legibility all checked, per #1210. Today: `identity-kit.ts`'s `generateIdentityDirections` builds the full seven-role variant set from a brand name and resolved tokens, and `adoptSuppliedMark` derives the same set structurally from a client-supplied SVG instead; `identity-checks.ts`'s `judgeIdentityKit` checks contrast, minimum size, clear space, and single-colour legibility against each (closes #1210). `master-mark.ts` still only validates a separately supplied mark's shape (three SVG documents). Neither generation path is yet wired into this package's checked CLI (no `designer-identity-check` bin) to produce `clossys/designer/assets/marks.json` for a real product.
